w:r.w:t: Complete end-state requirements with a zero-nice-to-have Launch baseline.
Approved direction; implementation details may be refined by engineering

Launch includes only capability essential to complete core work, support revenue or client delivery, prevent material data/security loss, meet a legal need, or replace no adequate manual/free/already-paid alternative.
Essential staff-built operating capability; additional non-payroll spend stays below £5,000 and is not a target.
Added only when adoption, revenue, risk or measurable workload justifies the staff time and cost.
COS progressively replaces third-party management tools while external networks and marketplaces remain channels.
Staff operational monitoring and KPI governance
Product, design, engineering, QA, Brand Circuit leadership
COS-CS-RPM-001 Roles & Permissions; COS-CS-WFM-001 Workflows & State Machines; Docs 4–10 in the COS pack
Every requirement is part of the approved complete blueprint, but its phase controls when it may be built.
Smallest usable internal system for Brand Circuit staff
Staff-built; less than £5,000 additional non-payroll spend; use free, existing or fixed shared subscriptions; no optional paid service
Added only when usage, reliability, client delivery or revenue justifies it
Requires a named trigger, estimated cost, expected benefit and approval
COS-owned capability that progressively replaces third-party management tools
Build only when strategically or economically superior; migrate safely, parallel-run and preserve rollback
is mandatory in the stated phase and testable.
means calculated from governed records rather than edited directly.
All IDs are stable. A deferred requirement keeps its ID when promoted to a later release.
Brand Circuit needs one controlled workspace to plan, produce, approve, publish and review content for:
external clients managed by Brand Circuit.

One client may own multiple brands. Brand Circuit controls staff assignment, workflows, approval configuration and operating standards. A separate Customer Platform will later expose appropriate requests, feedback and approvals to clients; it is not part of this module.
Brand Circuit workspace → Client/company → Brand → Campaign/plan → Content item → Channel variant/publish job
All records, searches, dashboards, exports, credentials and audit events must preserve this hierarchy. Cross-client access is denied by default.

w:r.w:t: Make every content item, owner, deadline, approval and next action visible.
Reduce missed deadlines, lost feedback, unapproved publishing and duplicated work.
Give management evidence-based staff and team performance visibility without invasive surveillance.
Create a clean operating record that can later power publishing, inbox, listening and analytics integrations.
Keep Launch cheap: staff time is also a cost, and no nice-to-have enters Launch.
The system must support configurable service-scope targets. The initial DELabs/Brand Circuit benchmark is:
5 publish-ready static or carousel assets per week; and
This is a seeded target template, not a hard-coded global quota. Targets vary by client, brand, period and role.
The menu order and names are fixed for this specification:
No area above is a separate COS module. “Command Centre” describes the Overview function and is not a twelfth menu item.
Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, LinkedIn, YouTube, X, Pinterest, Threads, Snapchat and Google Business Profile.
Static, carousel, short video, long video, story, text/thread, article/newsletter, live/event, poll/interactive and repost/UGC.
Creator discovery, outreach, contracting, commissions and payouts.
CRM, sales pipeline, customer support case management and lifecycle messaging.
Native replacements for Canva, Adobe, CapCut, Google Drive or broad analytics/listening tools at Launch.
Invasive staff surveillance, including screenshots, keystrokes, camera, microphone or covert monitoring.
Automatic disciplinary, pay, promotion, dismissal or other employment decisions.
The module may link to or exchange shared records with the relevant COS modules without duplicating their source data.
Portfolio status, risks, output and outcomes
Read across authorised clients/brands; no routine editing
Plan, assign, govern, approve and resolve exceptions
Protect client context, scope, approvals and delivery
Manage assigned clients/brands; no platform administration
Complete assigned copy, design and video work
Edit assigned records and submit for review
Operate authorised brand channels subject to gates
Read content records; edit governed performance records
Decide briefs, content, assets and publishing gates
Read/export authorised evidence; no silent changes
Review and decide client-facing approval requests
Basic secure approval page at Launch; later Customer Platform; never internal staff/workflow control
Job titles do not grant access. Access comes from customisable role templates and scopes defined in COS-CS-RPM-001.
Every operational record belongs to exactly one client and one brand; workspace-level configuration is the only exception.
A record cannot be saved without valid scope; moving it between clients is a restricted, audited action.
Default content lifecycle is Idea → Brief → Assigned → In Production → Internal Review → Client Approval → Scheduled → Published → Performance Review → Archived.
All standard transitions follow WF-CONTENT-01; no user can bypass a required gate through direct field editing.
Brand Circuit controls staff assignments, workflow templates and routing.
External/client identities cannot assign Brand Circuit staff or edit workflow/permission settings.
Approval routes are configurable per brand and content type.
A test brand can require both internal and client approval while another can lawfully skip client approval under an authorised, audited rule.
Rework returns the item to production without losing the rejected version or decision.
“Changes requested” creates a new work cycle and preserves reviewer, reason, timestamp and prior version.
Overdue and blocked are derived/exception flags, not hidden alternate workflows.
The item remains in its canonical stage while flags, age and next action are visible.
All significant actions are immutable audit events.
Actor, timestamp, scope, action, before/after values, item/version and outcome can be searched and exported by an authorised user.
Human approval is required before AI-generated work is published or an AI-drafted community response is sent.
No AI output can call a publish/send transition directly.
Brand Circuit uses existing tools before commissioning a paid integration or native replacement.
Every proposed paid dependency has a cost/alternative/benefit decision record and explicit approval.
No-code automations use Trigger → Conditions → Actions, are scoped per brand, testable, permission-controlled and logged.
A rule can be dry-run, enabled/disabled and traced from trigger through each action.
CCO/CEO involvement is exception-based, not a routine workflow substitute.
Normal items route to operating managers/assigned approvers; executive action requires a configured exception, reason and elevated audit event.
Show a scope-aware summary of due/overdue work, blocked items, pending approvals, upcoming content and critical alerts.
Changing client/brand scope recalculates every tile; clicking a tile opens the filtered source records.
Provide My Work and authorised Team View queues with owner, stage, due date, priority and next action.
Contributors see only permitted/assigned records; managers see authorised teams; counts reconcile to Pipeline records.
Provide an authorised Client View roll-up without exposing one client to another.
A scope test using two clients returns zero cross-client records, counts or search results.
Surface current-period production targets versus actuals, including the configurable weekly benchmark.
Target source, period, calculation and last update are visible; manual adjustments require evidence and audit.
Surface staff operational exceptions: inactivity on assigned work, missed deadlines, repeat revisions and approval bottlenecks.
Each flag links to source evidence and cannot itself trigger HR action.
Allow saved dashboard views and cross-client portfolio trends.
Saved views retain filters and permission scope; totals reconcile to source records.
Add predictive workload, delivery-risk and performance recommendations using native COS data.
Recommendation shows inputs, confidence/limitations and requires human action.
Capture ideas with title, source, objective, client, brand, audience, pillar, format/channel candidates, priority, owner and notes.
An idea can be created in under two minutes, searched, filtered and promoted without rekeying its metadata.
Promote an idea into a versioned brief using a brand/template-specific structure.
Promotion preserves the idea link and creates a DRAFT brief; the idea is not deleted.
Briefs must support objective, audience, problem/insight, key message, offer/CTA, deliverables, channels/formats, brand/claim rules, references, due dates, approvers and success measure.
Required fields are configurable; submission is blocked with field-level errors when required data is missing.
Support draft, submit, approve, request changes, reject, supersede and archive brief actions.
Actions follow WF-BRIEF-01; every decision includes actor/time/version and required reason where applicable.
Link briefs to shared Strategy & Planning and Campaign records when available, without duplicating their source fields.
A shared-record update appears in the brief reference; locally cached values are labelled and refreshed.
Provide comments, mentions and attachments/links on a brief.
Comments distinguish internal notes from client-visible feedback; permissions are enforced at read and write.
Generate suggested child deliverables/variants and repurposing tasks after brief approval.
Suggestions remain draft until accepted; accepted children inherit scope and trace to the parent brief.
Provide AI ideas, captions, scripts, CTAs, repurposing and brand/claims checks.
Input/output and model metadata are logged; cross-client retrieval is blocked; human review remains mandatory.
Provide native research, content opportunity and content-strategy intelligence.
Every generated opportunity cites governed internal or permitted external evidence.
Show the canonical lifecycle as a board and table with counts, owner, priority, due date, age, flags and next action.
Board/table filters return the same record set; lane counts reconcile after transitions.
Assign an approved brief/content item to one accountable owner and optional collaborators with due dates.
Only authorised Brand Circuit users can assign; reassignment records old/new owner, reason and timestamp.
Permit drag/drop only when the corresponding workflow transition and permission are valid.
Invalid moves are rejected with the missing guard; valid moves create one transition and one audit event.
Support task/checklist templates for copy, design, video, QA and platform preparation.
Completion rules can block review submission until mandatory checklist items are complete.
Support BLOCKED, ON_HOLD, OVERDUE and NEEDS_CHANGES flags with reason, owner and next-review date.
Flags do not overwrite the primary lifecycle stage and are searchable/reportable.
Record estimated and actual completion time, revisions, output volume and approval turnaround from normal workflow events.
Employees can see their data and challenge errors; managers cannot silently alter source events.
Add capacity planning, WIP limits, dependency management and automated delay escalation.
WIP/dependency rules are configurable by team/brand and do not change work without an auditable action.
Add native copy, design and video production workspaces while retaining the same item/task IDs.
Switching from external tools does not change the visible lifecycle or break historical links.
Provide month, week and list views of planned, due, scheduled and published content.
Views share filters for client, brand, campaign, channel, format, owner and status.
Display timezone explicitly and store scheduled timestamps unambiguously.
Two users in different timezones see labelled local time and the same underlying scheduled instant.
Allow authorised drag-rescheduling with conflict/approval impact warning.
The user confirms the change; previous/new dates and affected dependencies are audited.
Open the source content record and next action from any calendar item.
Calendar entries are views of source records, not duplicated events.
Detect channel-frequency, campaign, asset, dependency and approval conflicts.
Conflict rules identify cause, severity, affected items and resolution owner.
Synchronise relevant dates two ways with shared COS campaign calendars.
Sync conflicts are visible and resolved without creating duplicate records.
Provide one queue for brief, content, asset, schedule and exception approvals.
Queue supports scope, type, approver, due/overdue, priority and status filters.
Approval routes are configurable by client/brand, content type, channel and risk level.
A versioned route resolves the correct approver(s) at submission time and preserves that route with the request.
Reviewers can compare versions, comment, approve, request changes or reject with impact context.
Decision is bound to the exact version; material edits after approval invalidate or re-request approval under policy.
Support sequential and parallel internal approval steps with due dates, reminders and escalation recipients.
Overall status is derived from step outcomes; no unauthorised user can complete another approver’s step.
Provide a zero-cost fallback that lets authorised staff record an externally received client decision with evidence when the approval page is unavailable or unsuitable.
Recorder, channel, date, decision, evidence link and exact version are mandatory and audited; the recorder is not impersonated as the client.
Provide basic secure, expiring client approval links/pages with only client-visible context.
Recipient can review/comment/decide one request/version without seeing internal notes, other brands, staff data or credentials; revoke/expiry is enforced without a paid approval service.
Route client approvals and feedback through the separate Customer Platform using shared approval records.
The Customer Platform and Content & Social show one approval ID and consistent status.
Approval bypass/skip is restricted to authorised rules and always requires a reason.
A skipped step records rule/version, actor, reason and downstream risk warning.
Allow controlled bundle approval only for explicitly selected near-identical platform variants.
The reviewer sees every exact variant/version; each receives a separate decision; any later edit invalidates the affected variant approval.
Maintain an asset registry using existing shared-storage links, preview/thumbnail where free, metadata, owner, brand, format, rights and version.
Staff can find the authoritative asset without COS duplicating the original media file.
Support asset review statuses and allow production/publishing to select only approved assets unless an authorised exception is recorded.
An unapproved/quarantined asset is blocked at review/schedule gates with a clear reason.
Preserve version lineage and usage links from asset to content items/published posts.
Replacing an asset creates a new version; historic content still points to the version actually used.
Record basic ownership/licence, permitted channels, expiry and required disclosures.
Expired or missing rights produce a visible block/exception before approval or publishing.
Add managed uploads, automated metadata/tagging/transcription, duplicate detection, expiring share links and rights-expiry tasks.
Original file integrity, access control and audit are verified; automation output is human-reviewable.
Provide native, scalable storage, media processing, design guidelines, boards and usage maps.
Migration preserves IDs, versions, rights, checksum/provenance and rollback.
Provide a governed publishing checklist, platform-variant records, manual publish handoff/deep links and capture of published URL/time/status.
A user cannot mark Published without required approvals/checks and at least one destination result or authorised waiver.
Store intended channel, account, caption, asset version, CTA, tags, alt text, schedule and responsible publisher.
Published record identifies exactly what, where, when and by whom it was posted.
Integrate supported social APIs through the thin adapter layer for schedule, direct publish, result capture and failure retry.
Each publish job is idempotent, credential-scoped, logged and reports platform response/error without exposing secrets.
Support platform-specific validation and preview for all approved end-state formats/channels as APIs permit.
Invalid length/media/account constraints block scheduling and identify the exact correction.
Provide connection health, retry, sync logs, partial-publish handling and owner alerts.
One failed destination does not duplicate successful posts; retry targets only unresolved jobs.
Provide an authorised crisis pause for scheduled/queued posts by brand or workspace.
Activation requires confirmation/reason, stops eligible jobs, alerts owners and is fully reversible/audited.
Replace third-party social-management tooling where commercially justified; networks remain external channels.
Native replacement passes security/performance tests, parallel-runs, migrates history and retains rollback.
Provide a lightweight enquiry/action register linked to the source platform/thread, with brand, type, owner, priority, status and due date.
Staff can track a conversation to resolution without buying or building a unified-message ingestion service.
Distinguish internal notes from customer-facing response text and require human confirmation before any response is sent externally.
Internal notes cannot appear in an external-copy field/export by default.
Route sales, support, complaint, crisis and UGC opportunities to the relevant shared COS record or named manual owner.
Handoff preserves source link, context, consent/sensitivity indicator and audit trail.
Ingest permitted comments, mentions and messages into a unified, searchable thread view.
Messages retain platform ID, account, direction, timestamps and sync state; duplicate ingestion is prevented.
Add assignments, tags, SLAs, saved replies, AI response drafts, sentiment/intent suggestions and escalation rules.
AI/suggestions are labelled; sending remains permission-controlled and human-approved.
Provide native omnichannel moderation and conversation operations while external networks remain endpoints.
Provider replacement does not change conversation IDs or lose audit/history.
Maintain a manual signal/opportunity register for mentions, trends, competitor observations, risks and UGC.
Each signal has source/evidence, brand, theme, severity, owner, status and action.
Support configurable manual thresholds and critical-alert routing without a paid monitoring dependency.
A critical signal can be escalated immediately and traced to its decision/action.
Ingest permitted listening data from native APIs or approved fixed-price services; support queries, saved views, volume, sentiment and anomaly alerts.
Data source, coverage limitations, last sync and query definition are visible.
Convert an accepted signal into an idea/brief or route it to support/crisis handling.
New record inherits scope, source evidence and originating signal ID.
Add AI summaries and sentiment/theme classification with human correction.
Classification confidence and corrections are recorded; no autonomous public response occurs.
Build native listening/benchmark intelligence where lawful, technically feasible and cheaper/strategically superior.
Coverage, data rights, cost and accuracy meet the approved replacement rule.
Record content-level results manually or by CSV for each platform/measurement window.
Metrics preserve source, date range, currency/unit, entry method and evidence; duplicate windows are detected.
Show targets versus actuals for output, on-time delivery, approval time, revision/quality, SLA and available content outcomes.
Formula, weighting, target, source and version are visible for each KPI.
Generate weekly, monthly and quarterly role-specific scorecards balancing results, quality, speed, SOP compliance, collaboration and improvement.
Only equivalent roles are compared; raw activity cannot inflate a score without completed quality-assured output.
Permit employee comments/challenges and manager context without silent alteration of verified results.
Correction workflow retains original value, challenge, evidence, decision and audit trail.
Track workload/capacity, estimated versus actual time, output, revisions, approval turnaround, bottlenecks and inactivity from normal work events.
Employees see their own data; managers see authorised teams; no invasive capture is used.
Sync platform analytics and produce content/channel/campaign trends, attribution where supportable, recommendations and alerts.
Every metric identifies source and freshness; inferred attribution is labelled and reconciled.
Add the structured underperformance intervention workflow after separate approval.
COS flags evidence and supports coaching/actions; formal HR decisions remain human and outside automatic scoring.
Provide native analytics and recommendation capabilities that replace management/reporting tools progressively.
Replacement meets validated metric parity, migration, security, performance and rollback tests.
Authorised users manage clients, brands, users, scopes, role templates, teams and status/reference values.
Changes take effect only within authorised scope and are audit recorded before/after.
Configure brief/task templates, approval rules, publishing gates, KPI targets/weights, notification rules and basic listening thresholds by brand.
Configuration is versioned; existing records retain the applicable version/effective date.
Manage hidden encrypted credentials/OAuth connections for shared subscriptions and direct-tool handoff.
Employees use individual COS permissions; credentials never appear in UI or logs; revocation is immediate.
Provide an immutable, searchable, filterable and exportable audit trail with permission-controlled visibility.
User, timestamp, client, brand, action, before/after, item/version and success/failure/reversal are retained.
Configure in-app and email notifications available at no unnecessary added service cost; critical alerts may be mandatory.
Assignment, mention, approval, overdue, failure and critical events produce the configured notification/log state.
Track fixed subscriptions at workspace level, unavoidable variable usage and duplicate/underused subscriptions.
Cost view distinguishes fixed from variable costs and raises configured internal thresholds. Client charging is deferred.
Provide no-code automation builder, test mode, execution log and rollback/disable controls.
Provide integration connection health, retries, sync logs, credential-expiry alerts and adapter configuration.
An authorised admin can identify failed connector, affected scope, last success and safe retry action.
Internalise prioritised tool capabilities while keeping optional connectors/fallbacks.
Each replacement follows CS-BR-009, the replacement gate in §12.4 and Doc 6 integration contracts.
Enforce least privilege at workspace, client, brand and assigned-record scope.
Deny overrides allow; API and UI return the same authorised data/actions.
Support custom role templates that authorised admins can clone and modify.
Template changes are versioned/audited and do not silently expand existing users’ access.
Mask restricted fields/actions and explain why an action is unavailable without revealing sensitive values.
Restricted-state tests show no protected data in page, API payload, logs or exports.
Support time-limited delegated access and formal access requests/approvals.
Expired grants stop access automatically and remain auditable.
Significant creates, edits, transitions, decisions, exports, imports, deletes/restores, settings, credentials and AI interactions create immutable audit events.
An authorised auditor can reconstruct who changed what, when, where, from/to and outcome.
Notifications support in-app and email where available; assignment, mention, comment, status, approval, due/overdue and critical events are covered.
User preferences are honoured except mandatory critical alerts; delivery/read state is recorded when technically available.
Add push notifications, richer digests/escalations and full delivery analytics only when justified.
User/channel preferences and mandatory-alert rules remain consistent.
AI is optional, scoped by client/brand/user, isolated across clients and never directly publishes/responds.
Input/output/version history is auditable; disabling AI removes all AI actions for that scope.
Add AI asset tagging/transcription, listening summaries/sentiment and performance recommendations.
Human correction/approval paths and provenance are available.
Encrypt credentials/tokens, use OAuth where available, hide secrets from employees/logs and restrict connection changes.
Secret scanning and role tests reveal no plaintext credential; connection changes are audited.
Automatic daily database backup, 30-day retention, controlled recovery and periodic restore testing.
A test restore recovers selected records with documented result; restore action is permission-controlled/audited.
Add multi-region disaster recovery and advanced cyber-threat monitoring when justified.
Recovery targets and monitoring response are defined/tested before release.
Archive inactive records by default; deleted records enter a 30-day recycle bin; permanent deletion is restricted/confirmed/audited.
Linked active work blocks deletion; restore returns identifiers/relationships.
CSV export key records/reports and permit original asset download through the authorised storage source.
Bulk exports are restricted/audited, client/brand scoped and preserve IDs/dates/owners/statuses.
CSV import key records with template, mapping, preview, validation, duplicate detection, errors and rollback.
No invalid row commits silently; import can be traced and safely reversed.
Add advanced retention/legal holds and full workspace migration tooling.
Retention precedence and migration reconciliation are testable.
Permission-controlled global search across clients/brands, content, briefs, tasks, assets, posts, comments, approvals and users.
Search never returns unauthorised titles/snippets/counts; filters and quick-open work.
Add semantic search and search inside media/transcripts.
Results show source and respect the same field/record permissions.
Responsive web app for desktop/tablet/mobile, with tasks, calendar, notifications, approvals/comments, status updates, links/uploads and scorecards.
Current Chrome/Edge desktop and Safari/Chrome mobile pass the critical-flow test suite.
Provide installable home-screen shortcut; complex planning/reporting/admin remains desktop-first; no native mobile app.
PWA/shortcut opens the authorised responsive app without separate app-store build.
Use lightweight pages, basic autosave, clear connection/error status and safe retry for failed form submissions at no added service cost.
Interrupted edit is recoverable; retry does not create duplicate records.
Add full offline mode, resumable COS media uploads and dedicated compression only when needed.
Conflict resolution and upload integrity are tested.
Basic accessibility through standard components: contrast, readable text, keyboard/focus, labels/errors, alt text, non-colour cues and mobile zoom.
Critical workflows pass keyboard and basic automated accessibility checks without paid tools.
IDEA, BRIEF, ASSIGNED, IN_PRODUCTION, INTERNAL_REVIEW, CLIENT_APPROVAL, SCHEDULED, PUBLISHED, PERFORMANCE_REVIEW, ARCHIVED.

PARTIAL_PUBLISH, PUBLISH_FAILED and QUARANTINED are flags or child-record conditions, not additional default lanes. CANCELLED is a terminal exception state. Full guards and transitions are in COS-CS-WFM-001.
Content & Social references—not duplicates—authoritative records from:
Strategy & Planning: objectives, audiences, positioning and content pillars.
Campaigns: campaigns, offers, budgets and dates.
Customer Lifecycle/Sales/Support: routed leads, enquiries and escalations.
Customer Platform: requests, feedback and approvals when built.
Shared COS services: identity, permissions, clients/brands, assets, notifications, audit and staff performance.
Two-way synchronisation is used only where both modules legitimately edit the same shared record and conflict rules are defined in Docs 5–6.
Launch: link/deep-link existing Canva, Adobe, CapCut, Drive and social tools; avoid unnecessary paid APIs.
Scale: add required connectors through a thin adapter layer.
Native: redirect the same COS command/interface to native capabilities progressively.
Social networks/marketplaces remain external channels even when management tooling is native.
11. Staff operational monitoring and KPI governance
Individual/team trends, bottlenecks, inactivity and exception alerts.
Weekly, monthly and quarterly role-specific scorecards.
KPI formula, weighting, target and data source are defined per role and versioned prospectively.
Verified COS activity is used automatically where possible.
Manual entries require evidence and manager approval.
Managers may add context but cannot silently alter results.
Comparisons are only between equivalent roles.
Raw activity is contextual, not a substitute for completed quality-assured outcomes.
; automatic employment decisions are prohibited in every phase.
Launch is rejected if it requires more than the approved less-than-£5,000 non-payroll envelope without a separate user decision. The amount is contingency, not a spending target.
Native capability already available in COS.
Existing fixed-price organisation subscription connected/shared through COS.
Fixed usage bundle or annual plan.
Pay-as-you-go only where unavoidable and capped.
Vendor licensing and client charging are deferred decisions. Credentials remain hidden and access uses individual COS identities.
A Scale requirement may start only when its decision record identifies:
A third-party tool is replaced only when:
the capabilities Brand Circuit actually requires are ready;
native is cheaper or strategically superior;
historical data can be migrated safely;
old and new run in parallel before switch; and
Launch is accepted only when all of the following pass:
the 11 areas exist, with expensive integrations represented by useful manual/link-based Launch workflows rather than false “coming soon” actions.
a permitted user can take one item from Idea to Archived through every applicable gate using WF-CONTENT-01, including a secure client approval page and the manual-evidence fallback.
automated tests prove no cross-client leakage in UI, API, search, notifications, exports or audit visibility.
staff/client users cannot bypass permissions, approvals, required fields or Brand Circuit assignment control.
transitions, decisions, changes, imports/exports, deletes/restores, settings and AI actions are auditable.
My Work, Team View, calendar, pipeline, approval queue and scorecards reconcile to the same source records.
daily backup and a restore test pass; autosave/retry does not duplicate records.
critical flows pass supported desktop/mobile browser tests and basic accessibility checks.
no unapproved paid dependency or uncapped pay-as-you-go service is required to operate Launch.
DELabs or another OG brand completes at least one full weekly batch cycle, with user issues triaged through COS-CS-QAP-001.

Hosting provider, database, framework and specific external tools are engineering recommendations in Docs 6 and 9. They may not change the product hierarchy, phase gates, lifecycle, permissions, auditability or cost rules in this PRD without a recorded product decision.
